headings.text: At Portico, we’re redefining how career-focused institutions manage the student lifecycle.
Our technology combines enrollment, financial aid, and student success into one integrated platform.
Kimberly Verga, Senior Vice President of Operations, Managed Services
Mark Fuller, Director of Product Marketing
Natalie Gleason, Vice President of Marketing
Edward Crowder, Vice President of Information Technology
Tina Tran, Senior Executive Vice President of Customer Success
Danny Schwantes, General Manager of Payments

website.text:
With Portico, you get the tools you need, fine-tuned for schools like yours, to help staff work smarter and keep learners on track with their career goals.
Success isn’t just about getting learners in the door.
It’s also about preparing them for what comes after. By tracking employer relationships, placement rates, and program effectiveness, Portico helps institutions prove their value in the workforce and strengthen student-to-career pathways.
Portico unites four leading EdTech companies into the only fully comprehensive platform built specifically for trade and vocational schools.
Backed by decades of firsthand institutional experience, we deliver the software and services career schools need to overcome challenges and achieve key outcomes.
We prioritize the needs of our customers, ensuring our solutions truly solve their challenges.
We continuously evolve to provide the best technology for career-focused institutions.
We build trust through open communication, integrity, and accountability.
Doug leads Portico with extensive experience in the career education sector and a passion for helping schools recruit, train, and graduate the next generation of critical segments of the workforce. His professional background includes launching innovative businesses at global companies such as LexisNexis, and helping to build several early internet startups that now underpin the modern content and advertising ecosystem. Doug is motivated to equip schools with the tools they need to meet the changing needs of students and professionals in allied health, beauty and the trades.
Fun fact: Doug is fluent in Japanese and an active 911 paramedic on weekends.
Jeremy Chandler brings extensive experience in financial leadership, operational strategy, and business performance management. His background spans progressive finance roles at ARCOS LLC, where he advanced from Controller to Chief Financial Officer, along with earlier leadership positions at HBD Industries and Cranel. At Portico, Jeremy focuses on driving financial excellence, supporting organizational growth, and delivering strong outcomes for partners and stakeholders.
Personal pastime: Jeremy enjoys life in the Columbus area, where you’ll find him spending time with family, staying active, and engaging in his local community.
An innovative leader known for her operational expertise and compliance accomplishments within higher education, Siana has a 24-year track record overseeing Title IV operations for mid- and large-sized institutions, as well as those at Campus Ivy, which she co-founded. With over a decade of collaborative experience building market-defining financial aid software products, Siana’s revolutionary approach to financial aid servicing strategically leverages technology along with her deep industry knowledge.
Fun fact: Siana grew up in Jamaica and graduated high school at age 16 when she enrolled into the University of Miami.
Daphne Dor-Ner leads product strategy and development across the platform. She brings over 15 years of experience building learner-centered tools at institutions like Western Governors University and companies like Pearson, Lightcast, and Exeter Group. Daphne has also served as a higher education technology consultant, helping institutions ranging from for-profit to the Ivy League modernize their systems. She holds a Bachelor of Arts in cognitive science from Northwestern University.
Fun fact: She’s been learning to scull (lifelong learner at heart!) and claims to have ‘too many’ cookbooks.
Kimberly Verga leads Portico’s Title IV processing and compliance support for partner institutions. With more than 15 years in financial aid leadership, including roles as VP of Title IV Administration and Campus President, Kimberly brings deep regulatory expertise and a passion for student access. She is a NASFAA-certified Financial Aid Administrator and holds an Associate of Science degree from Middlesex Community College. Kimberly believes financial aid is a critical enabler, making education accessible to all students regardless of their economic background.
Favorite quote: “Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.” -Nelson Mandela
A seasoned education technology leader with 18 years of experience, Mark Fuller brings a wealth of expertise in building and marketing award-winning digital learning software for students and institutions around the world. His background includes driving product innovation, go-to-market strategy, and international expansion for prominent education brands such as Labster, Harvard Business Review, and edX, as well as consulting with dozens of publishing and instructional technology companies. At Portico, Mark uses his experience to deliver best-in-class software for students and leaders in career education.
Personal pastime: Mark lives outside of Boston, Massachusetts, where he enjoys Beantown’s food, live music, and sports scenes.
With his extensive experience in education technology and enterprise SaaS, Marc Barron leads Portico’s high-performing sales team, go-to-market strategy, and revenue organization. He’s passionate about helping institutions improve operations, align product offerings with workforce needs, and enhance student outcomes. As a co-founder of a leading career and technical education platform, Marc was critical in its success, building a strong sales infrastructure, finding the right market fit, and connecting cross-functional teams. At Portico, Marc oversees enterprise sales, specializing in GTM design and account-based growth. He is also an active mentor in the SaaS and EdTech sectors.
Personal philosophy: “Leadership should be grounded in a deep understanding of institutional challenges, and technology should solve real-world problems at scale.”
Natalie Gleason is passionate about transforming higher education through technology and storytelling. She brings over a decade of experience in edtech and B2B marketing to Portico, where she blends strategic vision with creative execution. Previously, she held senior roles at Mongoose, where she helped promote their pioneering student engagement technology, and Direct Development, where she worked on dynamic marketing programs to grow enrollment. Driven by the belief that education should be accessible and personal, Natalie helps schools adopt tools and strategies that truly support student success.
Fun fact: Natalie prides herself on being well-rounded. Great at parallel parking, 99% solve rate on the bonus round of Wheel of Fortune, and bakes (boxed) brownies to the optimal level.
Edward Crowder oversees infrastructure, systems architecture, and long-term technology strategy. He brings over 15 years of experience in enterprise IT, specializing in cloud migration, automation, and scalable real-time systems. Prior to Portico, he led engineering teams across both startups and global platforms. Edward holds a bachelor’s degree in computer science and is known for building strong, collaborative teams grounded in trust.
Personal philosophy: “A team that feels heard will go further than one that’s just told what to do. The job isn’t just to lead, it’s to listen.”
Tina Tran leads Portico’s customer success strategy, overseeing implementations and ongoing client support. With more than 15 years of leadership in academic operations, Tina brings deep expertise in SIS integrations, compliance, and institutional change management. She previously served as VP of Academic Operations at a multi-campus nursing school, where she led digital transformations and system standardization across states. Tina holds degrees in sociology, political science, and commerce and administration with a focus in HR management. Her background uniquely bridges institutional needs with system capabilities to ensure schools—and students—thrive.
Fun Fact: Originally from New Zealand and loves to cook – she’s currently making homemade butter.
Ahmed Hafeez is the Chief Technology Officer at Portico, where he leads global engineering, architecture, data, and technology strategy across the company’s SaaS platform. With deep experience in SaaS enterprise software, Agile methodologies, AI/ML innovation, and platform integration/modernization, Ahmed is known for transforming organizations and building resilient, unified technology ecosystems. Prior to Portico, he served as CTO at Veriforce and CAMP Systems, where he drove multi-platform integrations, scaled global engineering teams, and elevated development, quality, and product practices.
Fun facts: Ahmed is a competitive table tennis player, former cricket athlete, and proud father of two NCAA epee fencers. He’s a long-time fan of Calvin and Hobbes—often inspired by the quote, “If people sat outside and looked at the stars each night, I’ll bet they’d live a lot differently.”
Danny leads payments across Portico. He brings over 15 years of financial experience, 9 of them focused on Payments and FinTech. Experience includes working for processors such as FIS and Worldpay, and leading payment operations at Automattic (the creators of WordPress). His background includes strategy and optimization efforts, as well as defining GTM work and commercial negotiations, to implement the most well-rounded payments landscape.
Fun Fact: Danny always prefers working with his hands, whether it’s restoring classic cars, or finding the next home project to work on.
James Sonderegger leads client, partner, and employee training programs. He brings over three decades of experience evolving training programs and consulting teams for companies including Juniper Networks, Ericsson, Palo Alto Networks, and Alteryx. He is a published technology author, an agentic AI hobbyist with a Master’s degree in Information Systems, and a lifelong learner.
Fun Fact: When not building out role-based learning paths or researching adult education theory, he plays drums for a pop rock cover band in the Seattle Metro area.
Jen Miller helps companies grow without losing their humanity. As a senior HR leader in private equity–backed tech firms, she’s guided executive teams through mergers, rapid scaling, and culture shifts — always with a focus on aligning people strategy to business goals.
Known for turning abstract values into real-world behaviors, Jen builds systems that support performance, leadership, and connection. Her approach balances clarity with compassion, helping organizations operate as one team while staying grounded in what makes them unique.
Fun facts: Jen is a former competitive figure skater!

style. Each icon should use consistent line

Communication style:
Clear  
We’re simple, transparent, and honest.  
We work hard to build our customers’ 
trust. We explain complex concepts in 
plain language, avoiding technical jargon  
and making information accessible 
without sacrificing sophistication.  
When using industry terms, we provide

Thoughtful  
We’re discreet and take our customers’  
operations seriously. We demonstrate  
a deep understanding of their challenges 
while maintaining professional optimism. 
Our communication anticipates questions 
and provides relevant context without 
overwhelming detail. This voice cuts 
through complexity while maintaining 
authority, offering guidance rather

5.2 Typography
System Typefaces
When our custom fonts aren’t available 
due to technical limitations or licensing 
restrictions, it’s essential to use approved 
system typefaces as reliable fallbacks. 
When Proxima Nova isn’t available,  
Arial should be used. This offers a clean,  
modern sans-serif look that loosely  
resembles Proxima Nova for headlines  
and body copy.
If Hepta Slab is unavailable, Rockwell 
should be used. Rockwell provides a 
slab-serif appearance that maintains  
a similar strong and geometric character 
for subheads and calls-to-action.

print applications. While the primary  
emphasis is on the simplicity and legibility of 
the stroke, subtle accents from our approved 
color palette may be incorporated to  
enhance visual interest when needed.
